name: 1 Channel Zigbee Retrofit Relay

description.consumer:
Invisible upgrade. Instant intelligence.

Slip it behind your existing switch and everything changes — except the switch itself. Lights respond to your voice, your schedule, your presence. The wall stays familiar. The home becomes thoughtful.
description.technical:
A compact single-channel switching relay that retrofits any standard mechanical switch into a wirelessly controllable smart switch — no rewiring or hardware replacement.

Mounts behind the wall switch in a flush box or on DIN rail. Handles direct load switching up to 4A; loads between 4A and 10A require an external relay, SSR, or contactor. Communicates over Zigbee 3.0 with native Home Assistant support, and bridges to Matter and Apple HomeKit via a compatible hub.

Key Specifications
- Channels: 1
- Max Switching: 10A
- Direct Load: Up to 4A
- Protocol: Zigbee 3.0
- Compatible with: Home Assistant (native), Matter & Apple HomeKit (via hub)
- Installation: Flush box or DIN rail

⚠ For loads above 4A, an external relay, SSR, or contactor is mandatory.
description.long:
The Retrofit Relay is a compact wireless module that installs behind any standard wall switch — turning it into a smart switch without replacing the faceplate or rewiring. Once installed, it responds to schedules, voice commands, automation rules, and manual operation simultaneously.

With direct load switching up to 4A, it handles most residential lighting and small appliance loads with ease. For loads between 4A and 10A, it pairs with an external relay or SSR to safely manage higher-draw equipment. Communication runs over Zigbee 3.0 with mesh networking, meaning each relay extends the range of your smart home network.

Integrates natively with Home Assistant and supports Matter and Apple HomeKit through a compatible hub. Works alongside other Smartify devices — touch panels, sensors, dimmers — as part of a unified automation system. Ideal for retrofit installations where replacing existing switches is not practical or desirable.

name: 1 Channel Zigbee Retrofit Relay (40A)

description.consumer:
Built for the big loads.

Water heaters. Pool pumps. Heavy machinery. The 40A Relay brings your highest-draw appliances under smart control — scheduled, automated, monitored — without compromise on capacity or safety.
description.technical:
A heavy-duty single-channel switching relay rated for direct switching of high-current loads up to 40A — purpose-built for water heaters, pumps, HVAC compressors, and industrial equipment.

Installs behind an existing wall switch in a flush box or on DIN rail. Proper cable sizing, circuit protection, and qualified electrician installation are mandatory at rated current. Communicates over Zigbee 3.0 with native Home Assistant support, and bridges to Matter and Apple HomeKit via a compatible hub.

Key Specifications
- Channels: 1
- Max Switching: 40A
- Protocol: Zigbee 3.0
- Compatible with: Home Assistant (native), Matter & Apple HomeKit (via hub)
- Installation: Flush box or DIN rail
- IP Rating: IP20

⚠ High-current installation requires proper cable sizing, circuit protection, and a qualified electrician.
description.long:
The 40A Retrofit Relay is engineered for heavy electrical loads that standard smart relays cannot handle — water heaters, pool pumps, HVAC compressors, and industrial equipment. It brings the same wireless smart control to high-current circuits that the standard relay brings to lighting, but with direct switching capacity rated at 40A.

Installation follows the same behind-switch or DIN rail approach as the standard relay, but demands proper cable sizing and circuit protection at rated current. A qualified electrician is mandatory for installation at these power levels. Once wired, the relay communicates over Zigbee 3.0 with full mesh networking support, enabling scheduling, automation triggers, and remote monitoring of your highest-draw appliances.

Works with Home Assistant natively and bridges to Matter and Apple HomeKit via a compatible hub. Particularly valuable in Indian homes where geysers, submersible pumps, and heavy AC units benefit from scheduled operation and automated safety shutoffs. Pairs naturally with Smartify sensors for temperature-triggered or occupancy-based control of high-power equipment.

specs.compatibility: Home Assistant (native), Matter & Apple HomeKit (via hub)

name: 2 Channel Zigbee Retrofit Relay

description.consumer:
One device. Two circuits. Done.

A fan and a light. Two rooms. Whatever the pairing, each channel works independently — controlled together or apart. Fits behind your existing switches and disappears completely.
description.technical:
A dual-channel switching relay that converts two mechanical switches into independently controllable smart switches — no hardware replacement or rewiring.

Each channel switches independently up to 4A direct load. For loads exceeding 4A per channel, use an external relay, SSR, or contactor. Installs behind existing switches in a flush box or on DIN rail. Communicates over Zigbee 3.0 with native Home Assistant support, and bridges to Matter and Apple HomeKit via a compatible hub.

Key Specifications
- Channels: 2 (independent)
- Max Switching: 5A per channel
- Direct Load: Up to 4A per channel
- Protocol: Zigbee 3.0
- Compatible with: Home Assistant (native), Matter & Apple HomeKit (via hub)
- Installation: Flush box or DIN rail

⚠ Not a dimmer and not a dry contact output. Direct load switching only.
description.long:
The 2 Channel Retrofit Relay converts two standard mechanical switches into independently controllable smart switches from a single compact module. Each channel operates on its own — a fan and a light, two separate room circuits, or any combination — all managed through schedules, voice commands, or automation rules while keeping your existing switch plates intact.

Each channel handles direct load switching up to 4A, covering most residential lighting and fan loads. The dual-channel design means fewer modules behind the wall, simpler wiring, and lower cost per controlled circuit. At just 40 x 40 x 18 mm, it fits comfortably in standard Indian flush boxes alongside the existing wiring. Communication runs over Zigbee 3.0, contributing to the mesh network that strengthens whole-home coverage.

Integrates natively with Home Assistant and supports Matter and Apple HomeKit through a compatible hub. An efficient choice for rooms where two circuits share a common switch board — bedrooms with separate light and fan controls, bathrooms with light and exhaust, or any paired load scenario.

name: 1 Channel Zigbee Retrofit Dimmer

description.consumer:
Light that listens.

Full brightness for focused work. A gentle glow for winding down. The Retrofit Dimmer adjusts your existing lights to match the moment — behind the same switch you already know.
description.technical:
A single-channel phase-cut dimmer module that adds wireless brightness control to any standard wall switch — no replacement required.

Supports trailing and leading edge phase-cut dimming up to 200W for compatible dimmable fixtures and drivers. Installs behind the existing switch in a flush box or on DIN rail. Communicates over Zigbee 3.0 with native Home Assistant support, and bridges to Matter and Apple HomeKit via a compatible hub.

Key Specifications
- Channels: 1
- Max Load: 200W
- Dimming Type: Phase-Cut (Trailing/Leading edge)
- Protocol: Zigbee 3.0
- Compatible with: Home Assistant (native), Matter & Apple HomeKit (via hub)
- Installation: Flush box or DIN rail

⚠ Dimmable fixtures and drivers only. Not a 0-10V controller. Cannot function as a plain on/off relay.
description.long:
The Retrofit Dimmer adds smooth wireless brightness control to any existing wall switch without replacing hardware or rewiring. It installs behind the switch plate and enables precise dimming through voice commands, scheduled routines, scene presets, or manual adjustment — all while the original switch continues to function as a physical override.

Supporting both trailing and leading edge phase-cut dimming up to 200W, it works with a wide range of dimmable LED fixtures, halogen lamps, and compatible drivers. The dimming curve is smooth and flicker-free when paired with quality dimmable loads. Set warm low levels for evening relaxation, full brightness for task lighting, or let automations shift intensity based on time of day and occupancy.

Communicates over Zigbee 3.0 with mesh networking and integrates natively with Home Assistant. Bridges to Matter and Apple HomeKit via a compatible hub. Works seamlessly with Smartify scene switches and touch panels for multi-zone lighting control. Not suitable for non-dimmable fixtures or as a plain on/off relay — use the Retrofit Relay for switching-only applications.

name: Zigbee Shutter Module

description.consumer:
Curtains that follow the sun.

Morning light enters on schedule. Afternoon heat stays out. The Shutter Module brings your motorized blinds, curtains, and roller shutters into your smart home — responding to time, temperature, or a quiet command.
description.technical:
A single-channel shutter controller for AC motorized curtains, roller blinds, and shutters — providing interlocked directional outputs (Up, Down, Stop) that prevent simultaneous conflicting motor signals.

Installs behind the existing wall switch in a flush box or on DIN rail. Communicates over Zigbee 3.0 with native Home Assistant support, and bridges to Matter and Apple HomeKit via a compatible hub.

Key Specifications
- Channels: 1 motor channel
- Control Type: Interlocked directional (Up / Down / Stop)
- Max Load: 2A
- Protocol: Zigbee 3.0
- Compatible with: Home Assistant (native), Matter & Apple HomeKit (via hub)
- Installation: Flush box or DIN rail

⚠ Designed exclusively for AC motor loads. Not suitable for DC motors or use as a lighting relay.
description.long:
The Shutter Module brings motorized curtains, roller blinds, and window shutters into your smart home automation system. It provides interlocked directional control — open, close, and stop — with built-in safety logic that prevents simultaneous conflicting motor signals. Curtains can follow sunrise schedules, respond to temperature sensors, or adjust based on occupancy without manual intervention.

Installs behind the existing wall switch in a flush box or on DIN rail, maintaining the original switch as a physical override. The interlocked output design ensures the motor never receives open and close signals simultaneously, protecting the mechanism from damage. Rated at 2A, it handles standard AC curtain motors and tubular shutter motors used in residential and light commercial installations.

Communicates over Zigbee 3.0 with mesh networking and integrates natively with Home Assistant. Supports Matter and Apple HomeKit through a compatible hub. Combines naturally with Smartify light sensors, motion sensors, and scheduled automations for intelligent window covering control — morning light that enters on schedule, afternoon sun that stays blocked, and privacy that activates at dusk.

name: Analog 0-10V Zigbee Dimmer

description.consumer:
Commercial lighting. Unified control.

Large-scale LED installations deserve more than manual dimmers. This controller integrates professional lighting systems into your smart home — smooth, precise, and fully automatable alongside everything else.
description.technical:
A single-channel 0-10V analog dimming controller that integrates commercial LED drivers accepting a 0-10V input into a wireless smart automation ecosystem.

Outputs a low-voltage 0-10V control signal only — does not switch or dim mains voltage directly. Designed for DIN rail or panel installation. Communicates over Zigbee 3.0 with native Home Assistant support, and bridges to Matter and Apple HomeKit via a compatible hub.

Key Specifications
- Channels: 1
- Output: 0-10V analog control signal (max 20mA)
- Input Voltage: AC 100-240V 50/60Hz
- Protocol: Zigbee 3.0
- Compatible with: Home Assistant (native), Matter & Apple HomeKit (via hub)
- Installation: DIN rail / electrical panel

⚠ Control signal output only — does not switch or dim high-voltage loads directly. Compatible 0-10V LED drivers required.
description.long:
The 0-10V Analog Dimmer bridges professional-grade LED lighting systems into a wireless smart home ecosystem. Unlike phase-cut dimmers that modulate mains voltage, this controller outputs a low-voltage 0-10V analog signal — the industry standard for commercial LED drivers, architectural lighting, and large-scale fixture installations that require precise, flicker-free dimming.

The controller accepts mains voltage input and generates a clean 0-10V DC control signal (up to 20mA) that connects directly to compatible LED driver dimming inputs. This makes it suitable for recessed downlight arrays, linear LED fixtures, cove lighting, and any installation where the lighting driver expects analog dimming input. Mounting is designed for DIN rail or electrical panel placement alongside other distribution equipment.

Communicates over Zigbee 3.0 and integrates natively with Home Assistant, with Matter and Apple HomeKit support via a compatible hub. Fills the gap between commercial lighting hardware and residential smart home control — allowing the same automation rules, scenes, and schedules that govern standard fixtures to extend to professional lighting installations throughout the home.

name: Zigbee Gateway (Wired)

description.consumer:
The steady centre of it all.

Every device in your smart home connects through this. Wired to your network for rock-solid stability, the Gateway coordinates up to 128 devices — reliably, quietly, without a single dropped command.
description.technical:
A wired Zigbee 3.0 coordinator that serves as the central gateway for all Zigbee devices in the system — connected via Ethernet for stable, low-latency communication.

Supports up to 128 Zigbee devices with device pairing, scene automation, remote control, and unified device management through compatible mobile applications and automation platforms. Powered via USB-C.

Key Specifications
- Device Type: Zigbee Coordinator / Gateway
- Protocol: Zigbee 3.0
- Network: Wired Ethernet (RJ45)
- Capacity: Up to 128 Zigbee devices
- Power: USB-C 5V 2A
- Operating Temperature: -10 to +55 deg C
- Installation: Indoor, fixed LAN connection

⚠ Does not control electrical loads directly. A stable wired Ethernet connection is required for reliable operation.
description.long:
The Zigbee Gateway serves as the central coordinator for all Zigbee devices in a Smartify installation. Connected via wired Ethernet for maximum stability, it manages device pairing, command routing, and automation execution across up to 128 Zigbee endpoints. The wired connection eliminates the reliability concerns of Wi-Fi-dependent hubs — commands execute consistently regardless of wireless network congestion.

Powered by USB-C and requiring only a single Ethernet cable, the gateway maintains persistent connections to every paired device. It handles group commands, scene activation, and real-time status reporting without introducing latency or dropped messages. The Zigbee 3.0 protocol ensures interoperability with the full Smartify product range and other certified Zigbee devices.

Integrates with Home Assistant and compatible automation platforms for advanced rule-based control. Supports bridging to Matter and Apple HomeKit ecosystems through compatible configurations. Essential for any Smartify installation — whether a single room with a few retrofit relays or a complete home with dozens of switches, dimmers, sensors, and motorized window coverings.

name: Zigbee Gateway (Matter)

description.consumer:
Every ecosystem. One home.

Apple HomeKit. Google Home. Amazon Alexa. This gateway bridges them all — letting your devices work together regardless of which app you prefer. No compromises. No walled gardens.
description.technical:
A wired smart home gateway bridging Zigbee 3.0 and Matter protocols — enabling unified cross-ecosystem control through a single stable Ethernet connection.

Supports up to 128 devices with device pairing, cross-protocol bridging, scene automation, and remote access. Exposes Zigbee devices to Matter-enabled applications and Apple HomeKit natively via the Matter standard. Powered via USB-C.

Key Specifications
- Protocols: Zigbee 3.0 + Matter (IP / Thread bridge)
- Network: Wired Ethernet (LAN)
- Capacity: Up to 128 devices
- Compatibility: Matter apps, Apple HomeKit (via Matter)
- Power: USB Type-C 5V 1A
- Dimensions: 90 x 90 x 22 mm
- Installation: Indoor, fixed LAN connection

⚠ Does not control electrical loads. Communication and bridging layer only. Requires Matter-compatible ecosystem for cross-protocol features.
description.long:
The Matter Gateway unifies Zigbee devices with every major smart home ecosystem through the Matter standard — Apple HomeKit, Google Home, Amazon Alexa, and any Matter-compatible platform. Where the standard Zigbee Gateway coordinates devices within a single automation system, the Matter Gateway bridges them across ecosystems, eliminating the walled-garden problem that has fragmented smart homes for years.

Connected via wired Ethernet for stability, it supports up to 128 devices with cross-protocol bridging handled locally. Zigbee devices appear natively in Matter-enabled apps without cloud translation layers, meaning faster response times and continued operation during internet outages. The gateway handles device pairing, scene management, and remote access while maintaining the security and privacy standards of the Matter protocol.

Ideal for households where different family members prefer different ecosystems, or where Apple HomeKit integration is a requirement alongside broader Zigbee automation. Works as the primary coordination point for Smartify installations that need to coexist with Thread devices, HomePod, Apple TV, or Google Nest hubs as Matter controllers.

name: Convergia

description.consumer:
The brain behind every room.

Convergia does not just connect devices — it understands how they should work together. Every light, every climate zone, every scene runs through a single local platform that responds instantly and never depends on the cloud to keep your home running.
description.technical:
A locally hosted smart automation gateway that unifies KNX wired systems and wireless ecosystems — Zigbee, Wi-Fi, Matter, and LAN/IP — into a single interoperable platform running on an Intel NUC-based appliance.

All automation logic executes locally, ensuring reliability independent of cloud connectivity. Supports advanced rule-based triggers, conditions, and multi-step logic. Integrates AV systems and IP cameras directly into automation workflows. Web dashboard and mobile access included.

Key Specifications
- Architecture: On-premise (locally hosted)
- Protocols: KNX, Zigbee, Wi-Fi, Matter, LAN/IP
- AV Integration: Yes
- Camera Integration: IP cameras
- Automation: Rule-based, local execution
- Interface: Web dashboard + mobile access
- Hardware: Intel NUC-based pre-configured appliance

⚠ Does not switch electrical loads directly. Functions as the central intelligence layer. Qualified integrator installation recommended.
description.long:
Convergia is a locally hosted automation gateway that serves as the central intelligence for complex smart home and building installations. Built on an Intel NUC appliance, it unifies KNX wired infrastructure, Zigbee wireless devices, Wi-Fi systems, Matter endpoints, AV equipment, and IP cameras into a single cohesive platform — all processing locally without cloud dependency.

Every automation rule executes on the local hardware, ensuring response times measured in milliseconds regardless of internet connectivity. The platform supports sophisticated multi-condition logic — if a motion sensor detects presence AND the light level drops below a threshold AND the time falls within a specific window, then adjust lighting, set climate targets, and arm specific zones. AV integration means the same automation that dims the lights can lower the projector screen and route audio. IP camera feeds integrate directly into security workflows.

Designed for large residences, villas, and commercial spaces where a basic Zigbee gateway cannot manage the complexity of multiple protocols and dozens of integrated systems. Qualified integrator installation ensures proper configuration of KNX bus communication, network topology, and automation programming. The web dashboard and mobile interface provide ongoing access for daily adjustments and monitoring.

name: IR Blaster (WiFi)

description.consumer:
Every remote. Gone.

Your AC, TV, set-top box — all the devices that came with plastic remotes — now respond to your voice, your schedule, and your automations. Place it once. Forget the drawer full of remotes.
description.technical:
A Wi-Fi IR blaster that transmits infrared commands to legacy IR-controlled devices — TVs, air conditioners, set-top boxes, and other appliances — over the local network.

Connects to a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network and sends configurable IR codes via compatible mobile apps and automation platforms. Requires line-of-sight to target devices. Compact form factor for shelf or tabletop placement.

Key Specifications
- Protocol: Wi-Fi 2.4 GHz (802.11 b/g/n)
- Control: Infrared (IR)
- IR Range: Up to 8m
- Power: 5V DC 1A (Micro USB)
- Dimensions: 68 x 68 x 19.5 mm
- Installation: Indoor, line-of-sight placement

⚠ IR line-of-sight to target devices is required. Does not switch electrical loads. RF devices not supported — see IR+RF Blaster.
description.long:
The IR Blaster replaces every infrared remote in your home with a single Wi-Fi connected device. Air conditioners, televisions, set-top boxes, projectors, audio receivers — any device that responds to an IR remote can be controlled through voice commands, scheduled routines, and smart home automations. Place it once with line-of-sight to your devices and the drawer full of plastic remotes becomes unnecessary.

Connects directly to your 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network with no hub or gateway required. The compact form factor sits unobtrusively on a shelf or entertainment unit, transmitting IR commands up to 8 metres. Supports learning mode to capture codes from existing remotes, plus a database of common device profiles for quick setup. Scheduling means the AC can pre-cool before you arrive home, and the TV can power down automatically at bedtime.

Works with Amazon Alexa, Google Home, and Apple HomeKit through compatible apps and platforms. Particularly effective when combined with Smartify sensors — turn on the AC when room temperature exceeds a threshold, or power down entertainment systems when the room is unoccupied. For rooms that also need RF control of motorized curtains or RF fans, consider the IR+RF Blaster instead.

description.consumer:
IR and RF. Everything covered.

Motorized curtains speak RF. Your AC speaks IR. The IR+RF Blaster handles both — bringing every legacy remote-controlled device into one app, one automation, one home.
description.technical:
A Wi-Fi universal remote controller that transmits both infrared and 433/315 MHz radio frequency commands to legacy devices — TVs, air conditioners, projectors, RF motorized curtains, RF fans, and RF switches.

Connects to a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network and sends programmable IR and RF codes via compatible apps and automation platforms. IR requires line-of-sight; RF operates through walls within range. Multi-directional IR emission.

Key Specifications
- Protocol: Wi-Fi 2.4 GHz (802.11 b/g/n)
- Control: IR + RF (433/315 MHz)
- IR Range: Up to 8m (horizontal), up to 15m (opposite direction)
- Power: DC 5V/1A (Micro USB)
- Dimensions: 68 x 68 x 27 mm
- Installation: Indoor, within signal range

⚠ Does not switch electrical loads directly. IR requires line-of-sight; RF does not.
description.long:
The IR+RF Blaster combines infrared and 433/315 MHz radio frequency transmission in a single device — covering both IR-controlled appliances and RF-controlled equipment like motorized curtains, RF ceiling fans, and RF-based switches. Where the standard IR Blaster handles televisions and air conditioners, this dual-protocol controller extends smart automation to the full range of legacy remote-controlled devices in your home.

IR commands require line-of-sight to target devices with an effective range of up to 8 metres horizontally and 15 metres in the opposite direction thanks to multi-directional IR emission. RF signals at 433/315 MHz pass through walls within range, meaning motorized blinds in adjacent rooms can be controlled without relocating the device. Both protocols are fully programmable through compatible apps with learning mode and pre-built device databases.

Connects to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi with no additional hub required. Works with Amazon Alexa, Google Home, and Apple HomeKit through compatible platforms. The ideal choice for rooms where both IR appliances and RF motorized window coverings need unified control — living rooms with entertainment systems and automated curtains, bedrooms with AC and RF blinds, or any space where multiple remote types have accumulated over time.

A dual-function Zigbee sensor combining PIR motion detection with ambient light (LUX) measurement — enabling conditional automations based on both occupancy and brightness.

description.long:
The Zigbee Motion Sensor combines PIR-based movement detection with an ambient light level sensor in a single battery-powered unit. This dual measurement means your automations can respond to both presence and brightness simultaneously — lights trigger only when the room is occupied and actually dark, avoiding unnecessary activation during daylight hours.

With a 120-degree detection angle and 8-metre range, it covers a typical room from a single wall or ceiling mount point. The LUX sensor adds a critical layer of intelligence: a hallway light that only activates after sunset, a bathroom fan that triggers on motion regardless of light level, a staircase that illuminates when someone approaches but stays dark when ambient light is sufficient. These conditional automations reduce energy waste while maintaining convenience — the home responds when needed and stays quiet when response would be pointless.

Powered by a CR2450 coin cell with low-battery warnings, it installs in minutes with adhesive or screws. It communicates over Zigbee 3.0, joining your mesh network and extending its reach. Note that this is a PIR sensor — it detects motion, not static presence. For rooms where occupants sit still for extended periods, consider the mmWave sensor instead. For corridors, entryways, bathrooms, and anywhere movement is the reliable indicator of occupancy, this sensor is the practical and cost-effective choice.
